keys.statement: Simulators without a dividing-wall model represent it as coupled columns; the pump-around arrangement converges more easily than the four-column arrangement.

plain.title: Dividing-wall column does not converge: model it as a pump-around pair of columns
plain.when: Your simulator has no dividing-wall column model (one shell with an internal wall), and the coupled-column version does not converge.
plain.do: Represent the dividing wall with the pump-around arrangement rather than the four-column arrangement.
plain.why: The pump-around form has fewer interconnecting recycles.
plain.check: In CHEPTA, build the pump-around version and compare its products with the four-column one where both converge.

decisions.obstacle: A dividing-wall column that does not converge.
decisions.mechanism: Fewer interconnecting recycles in the pump-around form.

keys.statement: When an equation-oriented solver needs a good start, run a short dynamic simulation and use its final values as the initial guess for the steady state.

plain.title: Equation-oriented solve fails from poor estimates: start it from a short dynamic run
plain.when: An equation-oriented solver (one that solves all equations at once) fails from a poor starting point.
plain.do: Run a short dynamic simulation and use its final values as the initial guess for the steady state.
plain.why: A dynamic run moves all variables towards the steady state.
plain.check: Lab has not checked whether CHEPTA can run dynamically; if not, start from the closest converged steady state.

decisions.obstacle: A simultaneous solve fails from poor estimates.
decisions.mechanism: A dynamic run moves all variables towards the steady state.
decisions.operation: Initialise from a short dynamic run.

keys.statement: A dividing-wall column can match a two-column sequence's sharp ternary split with fewer trays, but with too few trays it needs much more reflux, and its liquid and vapour split ratios strongly affect the result.

plain.title: Sizing a dividing-wall column: optimise trays, reflux and both split ratios together
plain.when: You replace a two-column sequence for a sharp three-component split with a dividing-wall column.
plain.do: Optimise the number of trays, the reflux and the liquid and vapour split ratios (how flows divide either side of the wall) together.
plain.why: Fewer trays can match the split, but with too few the reflux rises steeply, and the split ratios set the internal flows.
plain.check: Scan trays and both split ratios and record reflux and duty at each point.

decisions.mechanism: Trays and reflux trade off; splits set internal flows.
decisions.operation: Optimise trays, reflux and both split ratios together.

keys.statement: Most of the energy saving of a fully coupled (Petlyuk) arrangement comes from the prefractionator doing only a rough split, which avoids remixing; a dividing-wall column is its single-shell equivalent.

plain.title: Three-component split: a prefractionator or dividing wall saves energy by avoiding remixing
plain.when: You separate a three-component mixture by distillation.
plain.do: Use a fully coupled (Petlyuk) arrangement, or its single-shell equivalent, a dividing-wall column, where the prefractionator does only a rough split.
plain.why: In a plain sequence the middle component is remixed, which wastes separation work; most of the coupled arrangement's saving comes from avoiding that.
plain.check: Compare the total duty with the best sequence of simple columns.

decisions.obstacle: Energy of separating a ternary mixture.
decisions.mechanism: Remixing of the middle component wastes separation work.
decisions.operation: Use a prefractionator or dividing wall.
